name: Doripenem

overview.mechanism: A beta-lactam antibacterial acting through inhibition of bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
uses: The historical US label lists complicated intra-abdominal and urinary tract infections caused by susceptible organisms; current Philippine labeling must be checked.

evidence.title: Historical US label: indications, renal dosing and restrictions

paragraphs.text: The August 2015 US DORIBAX label covers susceptible complicated intra-abdominal and urinary tract infections, including pyelonephritis. Its adult regimen is 500 mg IV every 8 hours infused over one hour when creatinine clearance exceeds 50 mL/min.

The label reduces dosing to 250 mg IV every 8 hours for estimated CrCl 30–50 mL/min and 250 mg every 12 hours for CrCl greater than 10 but less than 30 mL/min, each over one hour. These are historical US-label regimens, not independently proposed doses or confirmation of current Philippine labeling.
Hemodialysis removes doripenem, but the label explicitly states that evidence is insufficient to recommend a hemodialysis dose adjustment. No HD, PD or CRRT regimen is inferred here.

Doripenem is not indicated for ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia: the label warns of increased mortality in that setting. It also warns of seizures and reduced valproate concentrations with breakthrough-seizure risk; probenecid increases doripenem exposure by reducing renal clearance.

sources.citation: FDA. DORIBAX (doripenem) prescribing information, revised August 2015. Historical US label; verify the current Philippine insert.
